akhfash:7-7.t: He said ﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّاهَا﴾: He means "and the One who proportioned it" (وَالّذِي سَوَّاهَا). So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, swore by Himself, and that He is the Lord of the soul which He proportioned. The oath falls upon ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا﴾ [9].

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ﴾, that is: the she-camel of Allah — so beware of harming her (ناقةَ اللهِ فاحذرُوا أَذَاها).

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا﴾: followed it, rising when it sets,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلَّاهَا﴾ by its rising high,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَاهَا﴾: covers it with its darkness. «إذا» in the three [places] is purely adverbial (li-mujarrad al-ẓarfiyya), and the governing word (ʿāmil) in it is the verb of the oath.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَالسَّمَاءِ وَمَا بَنَاهَا﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَنَفْسٍ﴾, in the sense of «نفوس» ("souls"), ﴿وَمَا سَوَّاهَا﴾ in creation. «ما» in the three [places] is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun) or in the sense of «من» ("who").

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا﴾: He made clear to it the way of good and of evil. «التقوى» was placed later in observance of the verse-endings. And the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) is:

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ﴾ — the lām has been dropped from it because of the length of the speech — ﴿مَنْ زَكَّاهَا﴾: purified it from sins,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَقَدْ خَابَ﴾: has lost ﴿مَنْ دَسَّاهَا﴾: concealed it through disobedience. Its original form is «دسّسها»; the second sīn was replaced with an alif for lightness.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ﴾ their messenger Ṣāliḥ ﴿بِطَغْوَاهَا﴾: because of their transgression,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِذِ انْبَعَثَ﴾: hastened ﴿أَشْقَاهَا﴾ — his name was Qudār — to hamstring the she-camel, with their consent.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾ Ṣāliḥ: ﴿نَاقَةَ اللَّهِ﴾, that is, leave her alone, ﴿وَسُقْيَاهَا﴾: her drinking on her day; she had a day and they had a day.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ﴾ in that statement of his from Allah, upon which the descent of punishment on them was made consequent if they disobeyed him; ﴿فَعَقَرُوهَا﴾: they killed her so that the water she drank would be left safely to them. ﴿فَدَمْدَمَ﴾: covered over ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾ the punishment ﴿بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاهَا﴾, that is, the covering over them, that is, He encompassed them all with it, so not one of them escaped.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَلَا﴾ — with wāw and with fāʾ — ﴿يَخَافُ﴾ He, Exalted is He, ﴿عُقْبَاهَا﴾: its consequence.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَالشَّمْسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of swearing; ﴿وَضُحاها﴾: conjoined to الشمس.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿تَلاها﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:3-3.t: Conjoined to what precedes it, and the i'rab is similar.

daas-irab:5-5.t: Conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from mā and the verb is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: Also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿فَأَلْهَمَها﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿فُجُورَها﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿وَتَقْواها﴾: conjoined to فجورها; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أَفْلَحَ مَنْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the answer to the oath; ﴿زَكَّاها﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿بِطَغْواها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿إِذِ﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿انْبَعَثَ أَشْقاها﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿فَقالَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَسُولُ اللَّهِ﴾: fāʿil (agent), muḍāf to the Name of Majesty; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ناقَةَ﴾: accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr) by an omitted verb; ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَسُقْياها﴾: conjoined to ناقة.

daas-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَعَقَرُوها﴾: conjoined to كذبوه by the fāʾ.
﴿فَدَمْدَمَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾: agent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿بِذَنْبِهِمْ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿فَسَوَّاها﴾: a past verb and its object, the agent being latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿لا﴾ is negative; ﴿يَخافُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿عُقْباها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

dervis-irab:1-15.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَضُحاها) al-Qurṭubī said: "(الضحى) is feminine. One says (ارتفعت الضحى) 'the forenoon rose', above (الضحو); it is also treated as masculine. Whoever treats it as feminine takes it to be the plural of (ضحوة); whoever treats it as masculine takes it to be a noun of the pattern fuʿal, like (صرد)." Ibn Khālawayh said: "(الضحى) is a shortened noun like (هدى). (الضحى) is feminine, and its diminutive is (ضحية); but the better course is to say (ضحيّ) in its diminutive without the hāʾ, so that its diminutive does not resemble the diminutive of (ضحوة). (الضحى) is the face of the day. One says (ليلة اضحيان) when the moon in it is bright from its beginning to its end. (أضحى النهار) means the day rose. One says (ضحي فلان للشمس يضحى) when he came out to the sun and appeared. Allah the Exalted said: (وأنك لا تظمأ فيها ولا تضحى). Ibn ʿUmar saw a man saying the talbiya in a hidden voice and said to him: (أضح لمن لبّيت له), that is, make it evident. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشمس عارضت ... فيضحى وأيما بالعشيّ فيخصر
(She saw a man who, whenever the sun met him, would come out into the open, and who in the evening would be chilled.)"
And in al-Qāmūs: "(الضّحو) and (الضحوة) and (الضّحية), like (عشيّة), is the rising of the day; (الضحى) is a little after it; it is treated as masculine and its diminutive is (ضحيّ) without a hāʾ; (الضحاء), with a long vowel, is when midday draws near; with ḍamma and shortened, [it is the same]; (أتيتك ضحوة وضحى) 'I came to you in the forenoon'; (أضحى) means he entered it, and he made a thing appear; (ضاحاه) means he came to him in it."
(جَلَّاها) He made it appear and uncovered it.
(طَحاها) He spread it out, because what appears of it to the beholder is like a carpet, so this does not conflict with its being spherical. In al-Mukhtār: "(طحاه) means he spread it out, like (دحاه), and its pattern is (عدا)." And in al-Qāmūs: "(طحا يطحو) means he went far away and perished, and he threw a man on his face. (الطحا) is the level stretch of land. (طحى), like (سعى), means he spread out, and was spread out, and lay down, and went away in the land. (طحا به قلبه) means his heart carried him off into every matter."
(دَسَّاها) (التدسية) is diminishing and concealing through immorality. The origin of (دسى) is (دسس), as was said of (تقضض) that it became (تقضى), and as was said (قصيت أظفاري), whose origin is (قصصت أظفاري).
(فَدَمْدَمَ) He closed the punishment over them for their sin and destroyed them. al-Farrāʾ said: "The reality of (الدمدمة) is the doubling and repeating of punishment. One says (دمدمت على الشيء) when you covered it over." In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "(دمدمت الشيء) is when you made it stick to the ground; (دمدم الله عليهم) means Allah destroyed them; one says (دمدمت على الميت التراب) meaning I levelled it over him." Ibn al-Anbārī said: "(دمدم) means he became angry, and (الدمدمة) is speech that alarms a man." In al-Qāmūs: "(دمم الأرض) means he levelled it; (دمم فلانا) means he punished him with a complete punishment; and (دمم القوم) means he destroyed them, like (دهدم) and (دمدم عليهم)."
(عُقْباها) Its consequence and its outcome. In al-Qāmūs: "(أعقبه الله بطاعته) means He rewarded him, and (العقبى) is the recompense of a matter."

* I'rab:
(وَالشَّمْسِ وَضُحاها وَالْقَمَرِ إِذا تَلاها)
The wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive; (الشمس) is genitive through the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the omitted verb of the oath. (وضحاها) is conjoined to (الشمس); (والقمر) is likewise conjoined. (إذا) is for mere time, attached to the omitted verb of the oath. An objection has been raised that the verb of the oath is a performative (inshāʾ) whose time is the present, so it cannot govern (إذا), since that is for the future, and a difference of time between the governing word and the governed is necessarily impossible. It was answered that it is permissible to swear now by the rising of a star in the future, so the oath is in the present and the rising in the future; and it is permissible to swear by a future thing, as you say "I swear by Allah, when the sun rises", where the oath becomes binding at the sun's rising. The verb of the oath is of the present only when it does not depend on a condition. We have set this out usefully and fully in the discussion of Sūrat al-Takwīr. The clause (تلاها) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it.
(وَالنَّهارِ إِذا جَلَّاها وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا يَغْشاها)
The two clauses are strung onto what preceded and parallel it in i'rab.
(وَالسَّماءِ وَما بَناها وَالْأَرْضِ وَما طَحاها)
Likewise conjoined. (ما) in the three clauses is either maṣdar or in the sense of (من), and in any case it is conjoined to the noun before it, or the interpreted maṣdar formed from it and the verb is conjoined to it. al-Zamakhsharī rejected its being maṣdar.
(وَنَفْسٍ وَما سَوَّاها)
Likewise strung onto what preceded. The indefiniteness in (نفس) is meant for the genus, as though He had said "and any one of the souls".
(فَأَلْهَمَها فُجُورَها وَتَقْواها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (ألهمها) is a past verb with a latent agent and a direct object; (فجورها) is a second direct object; and (وتقواها) is conjoined to (فجورها). They differed over the meaning of inspiration (ilhām). Ibn Jubayr said: "He made it incumbent upon it." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "He made it known to it." Ibn Zayd said: "He made it clear to it." al-Zajjāj said: "He granted it success towards piety, and 'He inspired it with its immorality' means He forsook it." It was also said: He made it known to it and gave it a power with which both the acquisition of immorality and the acquisition of piety are possible. al-Zamakhsharī said:
"The meaning of inspiring immorality and piety is making it understand and comprehend that one of them is good and the other ugly, and enabling it to choose whichever of them it wishes." In this is an allusion to the doctrine of the Muʿtazila, who hold rational good and evil (al-taḥsīn wa-l-taqbīḥ al-ʿaqliyyān), that is, that good and evil are perceived by reason. The Sunnis, however, hold legal (revealed) good and evil, that is, that good and evil are perceived only through revelation, because they return to the legal rulings, without discarding the role of reason in perceiving the legal rulings; and in their view the knowledge of every legal ruling requires two premises: a rational one, which leads to the creed, and a revealed one built upon it, which indicates the specific ruling.
As for inspiration (al-ilhām) in the language, it is the casting of something into the mind. al-Rāghib said: "It is specific to what comes from the side of the Exalted and the side of the Highest Assembly. The Exalted said: (فألهمها فجورها وتقواها), so it is known that it is not specific to good but includes evil as well." In technical usage it is the casting of a meaning into the heart by way of outpouring without acquisition, so it is specific to good, since "outpouring" is not applied to evil, for which "whispering" (waswasa) is used.
(قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاها وَقَدْ خابَ مَنْ دَسَّاها)
The clause is the answer to the oath, and the lām was omitted because of the length of the speech. It was also said that the answer is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected". al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its implied form is 'Allah will surely destroy them', meaning the people of Mecca, for their denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as He destroyed Thamūd because they denied Ṣāliḥ. As for (قد أفلح), it is speech following His saying (فألهمها فجورها وتقواها) by way of digression, and is not part of the answer to the oath at all." (قد) is a particle of certainty; (أفلح) is a past verb; (من) is a relative noun, the agent; the clause (زكّاها) is the ṣila; and the agent of (زكاها) is a pronoun returning to (من). It was also said that it is the pronoun of Allah the Exalted, i.e. "he has succeeded whom Allah the Exalted has purified through obedience". (وقد خاب من دسّاها) is conjoined to the preceding clause and parallel to it.
(كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْواها إِذِ انْبَعَثَ أَشْقاها)
A resumptive statement, delivered to confirm what was mentioned about the success of the one who purified his soul, or whom Allah purified, and the failure of the one who corrupted his soul, or whom Allah corrupted. (كذبت ثمود): a past verb and an agent; (بطغواها), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (كذبت). The meaning of the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of their transgression". In al-Kashshāf he made it for seeking aid, figuratively, as in your saying "I wrote with the pen", meaning: they did the denying by means of their transgression. Both (الطغوى) and (الطغيان) are verbal nouns, but the expression with (الطغوى) was chosen because it better resembles the ends of the verses. In al-Mukhtār: "(طغى يطغى), with fatḥa on the ghayn in both, and (يطغو), (طغيانا) and (طغوانا), mean he exceeded the limit; (طغي), with kasra, is the same; and (الطغوى), with fatḥa, is like (الطغيان)." As for al-Zamakhsharī, he said: "(الطغوى) is from (الطغيان). They distinguished between the noun and the adjective in the pattern fuʿlā from the roots ending in yāʾ, by turning the yāʾ into wāw in the noun and leaving it unchanged in the adjective, and so they said (امرأة خزيا) and (صديا)." (إذ) is an adverb for the time past, attached to (كذبت) or to (الطغوى); the clause (انبعث) is in the position of a genitive, as the adverb is annexed to it; and (أشقاها) is the agent of (انبعث). What is meant by it is Qudār ibn Sālif, with ḍamma on the qāf, who is made a proverb for ill omen, so it is said "more ill-omened than Qudār"; he was nicknamed "the red one of Thamūd". It is also permissible that they were a group, and the singular is because the elative, when annexed, is the same for singular and plural, masculine and feminine. The wording of Ibn Khālawayh, in which he made a strange confusion, is: "If the masculine is (أشقى), then the woman is (شقواء), because it is of the wāw-class, as in His saying: (ربنا غلبت علينا شقوتنا) and (شقاوتنا). The (ها) is genitive by annexation. The plural of (أشقى) is (شقو), like (حمر) and (صفر); if you form a sound plural you say (أشقون) in the masculine and (شقواوات) in the feminine, like (حمراوات)." Ibn Hishām said in reply: "His saying 'if the masculine is (أشقى) the feminine is (شقواء) and the plural (شقو)' is not good, as he did not distinguish between the afʿal that is an adjective of an indefinite noun and the afʿal that follows the course of nouns and is an adjective of an indefinite noun only with (من), being either annexed or accompanied by (أل). The feminine in this case is (الشقيا), and the masculine plural is (الأشقون), and (الأشاقي) is permissible by analogy, just as you say (الأكبر), (الأكبرون) and (الأكابر); and the feminine plural is (الشّقى) and (الشقييات), just as you say (الكبرى), (الكبر) and (الكبريات)."
(فَقالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ناقَةَ اللَّهِ وَسُقْياها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (قال) is a past verb indeclinable on fatḥa; (لهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (قال); (رسول الله) is the agent; and (ناقة الله) is accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "leave off hamstringing her and beware of her drinking". A discussion of the warning will come in the section on Benefits. (وسقياها) is conjoined to (ناقة الله), i.e. "and her turn of drinking".
(فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوها فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ فَسَوَّاها وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها)
The fāʾ is a conjunction; (كذبوه) is a verb, an agent and a direct object. (فعقروها) is conjoined to (فكذبوه), i.e. Qudār struck her on her legs and brought her down, and they slaughtered her and divided her meat among themselves. (فدمدم) is likewise conjoined; (عليهم), the preposition and its genitive noun, are attached to (دمدم); (ربهم) is the agent; and (بذنبهم) is also attached to (دمدم), the bāʾ being causal, i.e. "because of their sin". (فسوّاها) is conjoined to (دمدم). The wāw is a conjunction and (لا) is negative; (يخاف عقباها) is an imperfect verb, with a latent agent and a direct object. We made the wāw a conjunction only to suit the reading with the fāʾ, which is also one of the Seven; although the parsers and the commentators say that the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) or resumptive; among those who said it is a conjunction is Ibn Khālawayh.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying (ولا يخاف عقباها) there is a representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya), on the view that the pronoun in (يخاف) refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which is the apparent sense: that He, Glory be to Him, does not fear its consequence, as kings fear the consequence of their deeds. The purpose of the metaphor is to humiliate and abase them. It is also permissible that the pronoun return to the Messenger, i.e. that he does not fear the consequence of his warning them, and the metaphor remains. al-Suddī, Muqātil, al-Zajjāj and Abū ʿAlī said: the wāw is the wāw of ḥāl and the pronoun in (يخاف) returns to (أشقاها), i.e. he rose up to hamstring her while not fearing the outcome of his act, because of his disbelief and transgression. (العقبى) is the end of a thing and what comes of matters in its wake. In this there is some remoteness, because of the length of the interval between the ḥāl and its owner.

* Benefits:
The warning (al-taḥdhīr): it is the putting of a noun in the accusative by an omitted verb that conveys alerting and warning, the verb being implied as suits the situation, such as "beware", "keep away", "avoid", "guard against", "protect yourself" and the like. The warning is:
1- Sometimes with the word (إياك) and its derivatives, as in (إياك والكذب): (إياك) is an overt detached pronoun in the position of the accusative as the object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "keep away" or "guard against" or "beware"; and (الكذب) is conjoined to (إياك), or is a direct object of an omitted verb as well, as before. You may also make the wāw one of accompaniment and (الكذب) a mafʿūl maʿahu.
2- Sometimes without (إياك) and its derivatives, as in (نفسك والشر) and (الأسد الأسد); their i'rab is as before.
3- Sometimes with the word (إياه) and (إياي) and their derivatives, when conjoined to the one warned, as in his saying:
فلا تصحب أخا الجهل ... وإياك وإياه
(So do not keep company with the ignorant man, and beware of yourself and him.)
The governing verb in a warning is necessarily omitted in three places:
1- That the thing warned with is (إياك) itself and its derivatives.
2- That there is a conjunction.
3- That there is repetition, as in your saying: (الأسد الأسد).
It is strange that al-Nasafī mentioned in his commentary that the saying of the Exalted (ناقة الله وسقياها) is an incitement (ighrāʾ). There is no doubt of its problematic nature on the apparent reading, because incitement does not apply to it on the apparent reading; what applies to it is only the warning.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسِ وَضُحَاهَا﴾. ضحاها: its daytime. Likewise His saying: ﴿والضُّحى﴾ is the daytime. [Read] with kasra [i.e. imāla] on الضحى in ضحاها and in all the verses that match it, even if the root of some of them is with wāw.
Of that kind are: تلاها, طحاها and دحاها. Since the sura began with words of yāʾ and kasra, those of wāw followed them. Had the beginning been with wāw, giving all of that fatḥa would be permissible. Ḥamza used to give fatḥa to what is from wāw and kasra to what is from yāʾ; and that is from a lack of insight into the ways of the Arabs' speech. When the wāw kind stands alone, you give it fatḥa; and when the yāʾ kind stands alone, you have a choice in it: whether you give fatḥa or kasra, it is correct.

farraa:2-2.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلاَهَا﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: I read all of it with kasra [139/a]. He means: it followed it, i.e. followed the sun. It is also said: إذا تلاها, so it took of its light. You would say in speech: "I followed (اتبعت) the opinion of Abū Ḥanīfa" and "I took (أخذت) the opinion of Abū Ḥanīfa"; following (الاتباع) and التلوّ are the same.

farraa:3-3.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا جَلاَّهَا﴾: it dispelled the darkness. A pronoun referring to the darkness was permissible though it was not mentioned, because its meaning is known. Do you not see that you say: أصبحت باردةً (it became cold in the morning), أمست باردةً (it became cold in the evening), and هبّت شمالاً (it blew from the north), using pronouns for feminine nouns that have not been mentioned, because their meaning is known?

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا﴾.
He made known to it the way of good and the way of evil. It is like His saying: ﴿وَهَدَيْنَاهُ النَّجْدَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن زَكَّاهَا﴾.
He says: a soul that Allah has purified has succeeded, and a soul that He has buried has failed. It is also said: whoever purifies his soul with obedience and charity has succeeded, and whoever buries his soul (دسّاها), making it obscure by abandoning charity and obedience, has failed. We consider — and Allah knows best — that دسّاها is from دسّست, one of its sīns being replaced by yāʾ, as they said تظنّيت from الظنّ, and تقضّيت, meaning تقضّضت, from the swooping of the falcon (تقضّض البازي), and خرجت أتلعّى: I went out seeking the لُعاع (tender herbage) to graze it. The Arabs replace a letter of a doubled [consonant] with yāʾ and wāw; of that is what we have mentioned to you. I heard one of Banū ʿUqayl recite:
* يشبو بها نشجانه *
[from النشيج (sobbing)] — this is the end of a verse — (his sobs make it show.) He means يَشُبّ: it makes it show; one says: الخمار الأسود يشبّ لون البيضاء (the black veil sets off the fair woman's colour); so he made it wāw. I have heard it in other cases too. One says: دَوِّيّة and داوِيّة (desert); one says: أمّا فلان فصالح and أيما. Of that kind is their saying دينار, whose origin is دِنّار; what indicates that is their plural of it, دنانير, and they did not say ديانير; and ديوان, whose origin was دِوّان, because of their plural of it, دواوين [139/b]; and ديباج: ديابيج; and قيراط: قراريط, as though it were قِرّاط. We consider that دسّاها is دسّسها (he hid it), because the miser hides his dwelling and his wealth, while the other displays his dwelling on the heights and the hills, so as not to be hidden from guests and whoever seeks him. All is correct.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿بِطَغْوَاهَآ﴾.
He meant: بطغيانها (by its transgression), except that الطغوى is more in keeping with the verse-endings, so it was chosen for that. Do you not see that He said: ﴿وَآخِرُ دَعْوَاهُمْ أَنِ الْحَمْدُ للهِ﴾, its meaning being: the last of their supplication (دعائهم); and likewise ﴿دَعْوَاهُمْ فيها سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ﴾ — their supplication in it is this.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذِ ٱنبَعَثَ أَشْقَاهَا﴾.
It is said that they were two: So-and-so ibn Dahr, and the other Qudār. He did not say: أشقياها (its two most wretched), though that would be permissible if it came; because when the Arabs [annex] the أفعل with which they praise, and into which (من) enters, to nouns, they make it singular in the position of the dual, the feminine and the plural. So they say for two: هذا أفضل الناس (this is the best of people) and هذان خير الناس (these two are the best of people), and they also make it dual. Abū al-Qumqām al-Asadī recited to me for its dual:
ألا بكرَ النَّاعِى بِخيرَىْ بنى أسد * بعمرِو بن مسعودٍ، وبالسِّيِّدِ الصَّمَدْ
فإِنْ تَسَلُونى بالبيانِ فإِنَّه * أبو مَعْقِل لا حىَّ عنْه، ولاَ حَدَدْ
(The herald of death came early with [news of] the two best of Banū Asad: ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd and the lordly chief. If you ask me to make it plain, it is Abū Maʿqil — none can stand in for him and none is barred from him.)
Al-Farrāʾ said: i.e. no living one suffices in his place, i.e. no one but he is called to [as] "حيّ على فلان"; and ولا حدد: i.e. no one is turned away from him, no one is deprived. Another recited to me with the singular, blaming two sons of his:
يا أخبثَ الناسِ كل الناس قد علموا * لو تستطيعانِ كُنَّا مِثْل مِعْضاد
(O most wicked of people — all the people know it — if you two were able, we would be like a [cutting] blade.)
So he used the singular and did not say يا أخبثَي; and all is correct. Whoever uses the singular for two also says for the female: هي أشقى القوم (she is the most wretched of the people); and whoever uses the dual says: هي شُقيا النسوة, on the pattern فُعلى.
Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī recited to me:
غَبَقْتُك عُظْمَاها سَنَاماً أو انبرى * برزقك براق المتون أريب
(I gave you as your evening drink the greatest of them in hump, or else there came forward with your provision one with gleaming back, skilful.)

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَقَالَ لَهُمْ رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ نَاقَةَ ٱللَّهِ﴾. You put الناقة in the accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr): he warned them about it; and every warning is accusative. [140/a] If it were nominative on an implied [mubtadaʾ]: "This is the she-camel of Allah" — the Arabs sometimes put it in the nominative while it carries the meaning of warning. Do you not see that the Arabs say: هذا العدوُّ هذا العدوُّ فاهربوا (here is the enemy, here is the enemy, so flee!), which carries a warning; and هذا الليلُ فارتحلوا (here is the night, so set off!)? So if a reader read it in the nominative he would be correct. Someone recited to me:
إن قوماً منهم عميرٌ وأشباهُ * عُمَيْرٍ ومنهُم السَّفَّاحُ
لجديرون بالوفاءِ إذا قا * ل أَخو النجدة: السلاحُ السلاح
(A people among whom are ʿUmayr and the likes of ʿUmayr, and among whom is al-Saffāḥ, are worthy of keeping faith when the man of valour says: "Weapons! Weapons!")
So he put it in the nominative, while it contains the command to take up arms.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوهَا﴾.
Someone may say: How [can it be] "they denied him and then hamstrung her"? We consider that the [expected] wording would be: "they hamstrung her and then denied him", so that the denial comes after the hamstringing. But it may be as he supposed; because you say: "They killed their messenger, and so denied him", i.e. the killing was denial enough. That is one interpretation. Or فكذبوه may be a self-sufficient expression, and His saying ﴿فعقروها﴾ a response to His saying ﴿إذ انْبَعَث أَشْقَاها﴾: so they hamstrung her. That is how the exegesis came. It may also be placed earlier and later, because the hamstringing occurred with the denial; and when two acts occur together, you may put whichever you wish first. Of that kind is: أعطيتَ فأحسنتَ (you gave and so did well), and if you said: أحسنتَ فأعطيتَ (you did well and so gave), it would have that same meaning, because giving is doing well and doing well is giving. Likewise the hamstringing is the denial; so you put first whichever you wish and the other later.
Someone may say: How did He say "so they denied him", when they had not denied him before that, since they accepted that the she-camel should have a drinking share and they a drinking share? It has come in the exegesis that they had acknowledged this without believing him. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَدَمْدَمَ﴾:
He shook [the earth] with them. ﴿فَسَوَّاهَا﴾ over them.
It is also said: فسوّاها: He levelled the nation; He sent down the punishment on its small and its great, in the sense that He made them all equal.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ يَخَافُ عُقْبَاهَا﴾.
The people of Medina read: "فلا يخاف عقباها" with fāʾ, and so it is in their codices; the people of Kufa and Basra [read]: "ولا يخاف عقباها" with wāw, which is better in [terms of] the exegesis, [140/b] because it has come [to mean]: he hamstrung her and did not fear the consequence of hamstringing her; so the wāw is better here. It is also said: لا يخاف عقباها: Allah does not fear that she will return and follow up after He destroyed them; with this meaning the fāʾ is better than the wāw. All is correct.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb أقسم (I swear); the time of the verb of the oath is the present, while «إذا» is a future adverb; it is permissible to swear now by the rising of the star in the future, and it is permissible to swear by a thing that will come to exist.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: It is permissible for «ما» to apply to individual rational beings, since what is meant by it is the Creator the Exalted; «ما»: a relative noun in the position of the genitive, conjoined to «السماء».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The clause «فألهمها» is conjoined to the clause {سَوَّاهَا}.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «إذ»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) {كَذَّبَتْ}.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «ناقة»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, i.e. (احذروا) (beware).

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «فكذَّبوه» is conjoined to the clause «قال».

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «ولا يخاف عقباها» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {سَوَّاهَا}.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying, the Exalted: (قد أفلح من زكاها): in (زكى) there is a pronoun referring to (من), by which the ṣila (relative clause) is completed, i.e. "whoever purifies his soul by righteous deeds".

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying (وقد خاب من دساها): i.e. he concealed his soul by evil deeds. It is also said that in (زكاها) and (دساها) there is a pronoun referring back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, i.e. "whoever Allah purifies has succeeded, and whoever Allah forsakes has failed". This is far-fetched, since then no pronoun from its ṣila (relative clause) refers back to (من); the pronoun refers back only to the name of Allah, exalted be His mention. But if you make (من) a noun for the soul, and use the feminine according to the meaning, saying (زكاها) and (دساها), it is permissible, because the hāʾ and alif then refer back to (من), so the speech is sound; as if in the implied form it were "the soul which Allah purified has succeeded, and the soul which Allah forsook and concealed has failed"; and the meaning of (دساها) is "concealed it by evil deeds". Or (من) may mean the party, the faction or the group, so the hāʾ in (زكاها) and (دساها) refers back to (من), and the speech is good with the pronoun [of the verbs] in (زكاها) and (دساها) being for Allah, exalted be His mention. The origin of (دساها) is (دسسها), from "I hid (دسست) the thing" when you concealed it; but they replaced the last sīn with a yāʾ, and it turned into an alif because it was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa.

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His saying (ناقة الله): accusative by way of incitement/warning (al-ighrāʾ), i.e. "beware of the she-camel of Allah". (وسقياها) is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to (ناقة).

mekki-muskil:14-14.t: His saying (فسواها): the hāʾ refers back to the destruction (الدمدمة), which His saying (فدمدم) indicates, i.e. He made them equal in the punishment.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His saying (فلا يخاف عقباها): whoever reads it with fāʾ, the verb belongs to Allah, exalted be His mention. Whoever reads it with wāw, the verb belongs to the one who hamstrung [the she-camel], i.e. "their most wretched one rose up and did not fear its consequence". It is also possible that whoever reads it with wāw makes the verb belong to Allah, as with the fāʾ.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿والشمس﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and genitive, and «الشمس» is the thing sworn by, genitive (majrūr); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath.
﴿وضحاها﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «ضحاها» is conjoined to «الشمس», genitive by an implied (muqaddar) kasra, and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿والقمر﴾: likewise conjoined to «الشمس», genitive (majrūr).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath.
﴿تلاها﴾: a past verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the pronoun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿تلاها﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿والنهار﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿الشمس﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath.
﴿جلاها﴾: a past verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the pronoun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿جلاها﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿والليل﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿الشمس﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb of future time, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb of oath.
﴿يغشاها﴾: an imperfect verb and a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the pronoun is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿يغشاها﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿والسماء﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿الشمس﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun conjoined to ﴿السماء﴾, genitive, the implied sense being: ﴿والسماء والذي بناها﴾ ("and the sky and the One who built it"). Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and it together with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to ﴿السماء﴾, genitive, the implied sense being: ﴿والسماء وبنائها﴾ ("and the sky and its building").
﴿بناها﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), and the pronoun is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿بناها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿والأرض﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿الشمس﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun conjoined to ﴿الأرض﴾, genitive. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and it together with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to ﴿الأرض﴾, genitive.
﴿طحاها﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), and the pronoun is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿طحاها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ونفس﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿الشمس﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and ﴿ما﴾ is a relative noun conjoined to ﴿نفس﴾, genitive. Or ﴿ما﴾ is maṣdariyya, and it together with what follows is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun); the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to ﴿نفس﴾, genitive.
﴿سواها﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), and the pronoun is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿سواها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فألهمها﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «ألهمها» is a past verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فجورها﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, and the pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وتقواها﴾: conjoined to ﴿فجورها﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿ألهمها﴾ is conjoined to ﴿سواها﴾.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿قد﴾: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
﴿أفلح﴾: a past verb.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿زكاها﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), referring back to ﴿من﴾, and ﴿ها﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿زكاها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. The clause is the answer of the oath; and it was said: the answer is omitted, its implied form being "you will surely be resurrected" (لتبعثن), and the clause ﴿قد أفلح﴾ follows on from His saying ﴿فألهمها﴾.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وقد﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and «قد» is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
﴿خاب﴾: a past verb.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿دساها﴾: a past verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir), referring back to ﴿من﴾; and it was said: it refers back to Allah the Exalted, i.e. "ruined is the one whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made wretched"; and ﴿ها﴾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿دساها﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position, and the clause is conjoined to the one before it.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿كذبت﴾: resumptive speech, with no grammatical position; «كذبت» is a past verb, and the tāʾ is of the feminine.
﴿ثمود﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿بطغواها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إذ﴾: an adverb of past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿كذبت﴾ or to ﴿طغواها﴾.
﴿انبعث﴾: a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿أشقاها﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿انبعث﴾ is in the position of genitive by the adverb being annexed to it.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿فقال﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «قال» is a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قال﴾.
﴿رسول﴾: fāʿil (agent).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ناقة﴾: accusative (manṣūb) by way of warning (taḥdhīr), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "leave off hamstringing her" (ذروا عقرها); the clause ﴿ناقة الله﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وسقياها﴾: conjoined to ﴿ناقة الله﴾, accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, i.e. "and her drinking" (وشربها); the clause ﴿فقال لهم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿كذبت﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿فكذبوه﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and «كذبوه» is a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿فكذبوه﴾ is conjoined to ﴿قال لهم﴾.
﴿فعقروها﴾: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, and it is conjoined to ﴿فكذبوه﴾.
﴿فدمدم﴾: a past verb, conjoined.
﴿عليهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿دمدم﴾.
﴿ربهم﴾: fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿بذنبهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿دمدم﴾, and the bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of their sin" (بسبب ذنبهم).
﴿فسواها﴾: a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi, conjoined to ﴿دمدم﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, or circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or resumptive, and «لا» is negating.
﴿يخاف﴾: an imperfect verb, and the agent is latent (mustatir).
﴿عقباها﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa, and the pronoun is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿ولا يخاف...﴾ is conjoined, or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: What is well known in the language is that al-ḍuḥā is the first rising of the sun when it shines forth, even though Mujāhid said: al-ḍuḥā is the daytime, and that is the view of al-Farrāʾ.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
"…and (has failed whose soul He) led astray". Qatāda said: he has succeeded who purified his soul with righteous deeds. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this there is an obscure point of grammar that al-Farrāʾ did not mention, even though he mentioned the two views on the meaning. It is that if the pronoun refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, nothing from its ṣila (relative clause) refers back to من except through a far-fetched device. That is because if you take it as "the person who purified the soul has succeeded", nothing from its ṣila refers back to الذي; and if you take it as "the person whose soul Allah purified has succeeded", it is not permissible to use a pronoun for the soul, because nothing refers back to the soul. And if you took «من» as standing for the soul, it would be far-fetched, because من hardly occurs in the like of this. The device by which it is permissible is to construe it according to the meaning: that «من» is treated as feminine in the sense of "the soul", or that the meaning is "the group whom Allah purified has succeeded", so that «من» is for the plural. The meaning of "Allah purified it" is: He cleansed it by granting success to obey Him.
And "so-and-so purified (zakkā) his wealth": concerning its derivation there are two views. One of them is that it is from zakā al-zarʿ, when the crop increases and grows, i.e., his wealth became abundant through his paying the zakāt. The other view, which is clear and good, is that zakkā his wealth means he purified it and cleared it by taking out the shares of the poor from it. From this is أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْساً زَكِيَّةً [al-Kahf: 74], i.e., pure, cleansed of sins; and from it, "a pure servant (ʿabd zakiyy)", i.e., clean.
«وقد خاب», i.e., he did not attain what he wanted, whose soul Allah corrupted (dassā), i.e., abandoned it so it committed sins. And on the other view, "who corrupted his soul", i.e., concealed it for committing sin. Its derivation is from dassa and dassasa, and one of the two sīns was changed into a yāʾ, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 568- رأت رجلا أيما إذا الشّمس عارضت ("She saw a man who, whenever the sun faced him…"), meaning أمّا.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِطَغْواها (11): al-ṭaghwā and al-ṭughyān (transgression) are one, except that ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: بطغواها means "by its punishment", al-ṭaghwā being a name for the punishment. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is valid on the basis of an omission, i.e., "by the punishment of its transgression", like وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ [Yūsuf: 82].

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
Al-Farrāʾ reported that they were two, and he recited: [al-Ṭawīl] 569-
ألا بكّر النّاعي بخيري بني أسد ... بعمرو بن مسعود وبالسّيّد الصّمد
(The announcer of death came early with news of the two best of Banū Asad: ʿAmr ibn Masʿūd and the lofty chief.)
He means that he made خير (a singular form) the predicate for two, and he likened it to their saying: "these two are the most excellent of people" and "these two are the best of people". Abū Jaʿfar said: What he reported is contrary to what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said, what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and what the exegetes said. Allah said: أشقاها, informing about one, yet he reported that they were two. And the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A man volunteered for it", and he did not say "two men". And the exegetes said: Qudār ibn Sālif volunteered for it. Abū Jaʿfar said: He has a parallel to it, or something greater than it, in Sūrat al-Raḥmān.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: I.e., beware of the she-camel of Allah. Al-Farrāʾ said: if a reader were to read «ناقة الله» in the nominative, i.e., "this is the she-camel of Allah", it would be permissible. Abū Jaʿfar said: Innovation in the readings is not permissible.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَعَقَرُوها: al-Farrāʾ said: He meant "so they hamstrung her and denied him". This is a mistake regarding the fāʾ, because it indicates that the second comes after the first, and this is the reverse of the language. Moreover, there is no situation here that compels one to it, because they denied Ṣāliḥ when he said to them: "If you hamstring her, Allah will take vengeance on you", so they denied him in what he said and hamstrung her. And it has been said: «فكذبوه» is a complete statement, then فعقروها is conjoined to it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the difficulties in this is that it might be said: they had believed and affirmed (him), and had assigned to the she-camel a day and to themselves a day for drinking. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the answer to this is that they acknowledged him but did not believe. This view he stated is one that ought not to be ventured except by a narration, because it is a matter of the unseen, and the narration is contrary to it. Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: The Uḥaymir of Thamūd held back from hamstringing the she-camel until they all gathered with him in denying Ṣāliḥ — their young and old, their males and females — and for this reason Allah made the punishment general. فَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ بِذَنْبِهِمْ: al-Farrāʾ said: i.e., He caused (the earth) to quake; and others said: i.e., He punished them. فَسَوَّاها: Abū Jaʿfar said: I asked ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān about this pronoun and he said: it refers back to the dumduma (destruction) which دمدم indicated; and someone else said: i.e., He made them equal in the punishment and destroyed them all.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
Thus read the people of Basra and the people of Kufa, and the people of the Ḥijāz read وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها [Translator's note: the printed vowelling is identical; the Ḥijāzī reading (and that of Ibn ʿĀmir) is فَلا يَخافُ with fāʾ, as the following discussion shows]. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the wāw is better. This is a grave thing to say — that it be said, of what the community read and what appears in the codex (al-sawād) transmitted from the Companions who took it from the Prophet ﷺ, "better" or "best".
Both readings were transmitted by the many from the many, so they are on the level of two verses, because their meanings differ.
Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad Nifṭawayh say: whoever reads with fāʾ, the meaning is for Allah, nothing else. And this is as he said; the exegetes hold this, and it is authentic from Ibn ʿAbbās. Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad said: and whoever reads with wāw holds that the meaning is for the one who hamstrung her, i.e., "the most wretched of them rose up, not fearing its consequence", i.e., and this was his state. What he said is good, except that with the wāw it may not be for Allah, Mighty and Majestic [Translator's note: so the text]. What he said is clear, and Allah knows best what He intended.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: What is well known in the language is that تلاها means "followed it", even though al-Farrāʾ reported that تلاها means "took from it", holding that the moon takes from the light of the sun.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
وَالنَّهارِ إِذا جَلَّاها (3): the apparent and clear meaning is: when it displays the sun, i.e., when it makes it manifest and shows it, because the sun is only ever in it (the daytime); even though al-Farrāʾ said: and the day when it dispels the darkness.
This is a far-fetched view, because the darkness has not been mentioned before.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: The pronoun refers back to the sun as well.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: وَالسَّماءِ وَما بَناها (5): ما is in the position of the genitive, i.e., "and its building" [Translator's note: i.e., ما is maṣdariyya], and likewise وَالْأَرْضِ وَما طَحاها (6). Ismāʿīl narrated from Abū Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ: طحاها means "spread it out"; and Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: طحاها means "divided it".

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: I.e., its fashioning. Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever said that the meaning is "the One who fashioned it", meaning Allah, Mighty and Majestic — if it were as he said, it would have been ومن.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "He has succeeded whose soul Allah has purified".

safi-cedvel:15-15.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is circumstantial (ḥāl) — or resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya) — (لا) is negating, and the fāʿil (agent) of (يخاف) is a pronoun referring to the agent of سوّاها, i.e. Allah [Note: It is possible that it refers to the warning Messenger, or to the one who hamstrung the she-camel.].
Clause: «لا يخاف ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from the agent of سوّاها [Note: It is possible that it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(يخاف): it contains an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is يخوف — with fatḥa on the wāw — its maṣdar (verbal noun) is الخوف. The vowel of the wāw was transferred to the khāʾ, then the wāw was changed to alif because the preceding letter has fatḥa.
(عقباها): a noun meaning the consequence of a matter, or its outcome; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma on the first letter and sukūn on the second.

* Rhetoric:
Representative metaphor (isti'āra tamthīliyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَلا يَخافُ عُقْباها».
That is, its outcome and its consequence, just as punishing kings fear the outcome and consequence of what they do. It is a representative metaphor, expressing their humiliation and that they are abased before Allah, Majestic is His Majesty.

safi-cedvel:1-8.t:
* I'rab:
(والشمس) is attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم). (إذا) is an adverb stripped of the conditional sense, in the position of accusative, attached to the implied verb أقسم, and likewise in the next two places. (ما) is a maṣdar particle «[Note: if it is permissible to use (ما) for rational beings or for individuals of those with knowledge, it is a relative noun in the position of genitive conjoined to السماء, and likewise in the next two places]» in the three places. (الفاء) is a conjunction ...
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما بناها..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to السماء.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما طحاها..) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to الأرض.
And the interpreted maṣdar (ما سوّاها) is in the position of genitive, conjoined to نفس.
Clause: « (أقسم) بالشمس ... » has no grammatical position (inceptive).
And the clause: «تلاها ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «جلّاها ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يغشاها ... » is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «بناها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما), the first).
And the clause: «طحاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما), the second).
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the particle-like relative (ما), the third).
And the clause: «ألهمها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause سوّاها) ... The answer to the oath is omitted, its implied form being "You will surely be raised" «[Note: or "Allah will surely destroy the disbelievers of Mecca" — as in al-Kashshāf — and it may be that the answer to the oath is the clause قد أفلح ... — in verse (9) of this sūra — with the lām omitted because of the length of the speech]».

* Morphology:
(2) تلاها: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is تلوها — its imperfect is يتلو, with fatḥa on the wāw — and when the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa it was changed into alif.
(3) جلّاها: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is جلّيها — with the yāʾ vowelled with fatḥa — and the yāʾ was changed into alif because it was vowelled after a fatḥa.
(6) طحاها: i.e. "He spread it out". It contains a weakening by substitution; it is said that the original is طحوها, and it is said طحيها. In al-Qāmūs: طحا like سعى means "to spread out"; and طحا يطحو means "to be far away", "to perish", and "to throw a person on his face"; and الطحا is the flat part of the earth.
(8) فجور: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral فجر; its wazn is فعول (with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn).

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(قد) is a particle of confirmation in both places. (من) is a relative noun in the position of accusative as a direct object in both places ..
Clause: «قد أفلح من ... » has no grammatical position (explanatory resumptive) «[Note: or it is the answer to the oath, with the lām omitted because of the length of the speech]».
And the clause: «زكّاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative noun (من)).
And the clause: «قد خاب من ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: «دسّاها ... » has no grammatical position (ṣila of the second relative noun (من)).

* Morphology:
(9) زكّاها: it contains a weakening by substitution; the ʿayn of the verb in its bare form is a wāw, which was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(10) خاب: it contains a weakening by substitution; the original is خيب — its imperfect is يخيب — the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa and was changed into alif.
(دسّاها) it is said that the alif is converted from a sīn and the original is دسّسها — with three sīns — and when similar letters followed one another, the sīn was changed into yāʾ, then a weakening by substitution took place in it. The lexicographers said: the original is دسّسها from التدسيس, which is hiding a thing within a thing, so its sīn was replaced by a yāʾ.

safi-cedvel:11-14.t:
* I'rab:
(بطغواها) is attached to (كذّبت), and the (باء) is of causality, or of figurative instrumentality. (إذ) is an adverb in the position of accusative, attached to (كذّبت). (الفاء) is a conjunction. (لهم) is attached to (قال). (ناقة) is a direct object of an omitted verb in the manner of warning (taḥdhīr), i.e. "leave the she-camel of Allah", i.e. "beware of hamstringing her". (سقياها) is conjoined to ناقة, accusative.
Clause: «كذّبت ثمود» has no grammatical position (resumptive).
And the clause: «انبعث أشقاها» is in the position of genitive as a muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «قال لهم رسول ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the resumptive clause).
And the clause: « (ذروا) ناقة الله ... » is in the position of accusative as the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
Verse 14: (الفاء) is a conjunction in the four places. (عليهم) is attached to (دمدم), meaning "He covered over". (بذنبهم) is attached to (دمدم), and the (باء) is of causality.
And the clause: «كذّبوه ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause قال لهم).
And the clause: «عقروها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause كذّبوه).
And the clause: «دمدم عليهم ربّهم ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause عقروها).
And the clause: «سوّاها ... » has no grammatical position (conjoined to the clause دمدم).

* Morphology:
(11) طغواها: a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral طغا يطغو (the pattern of نصر) and طغى يطغى (the pattern of فتح); its wazn is فعلى.
(13) سقياها: the noun from السقي, or what is used to give drink; its wazn is فعلى (with ḍamma and sukūn). The alif in (السقيا) is written long because a yāʾ precedes it.

* Benefits:
- Incitement (ighrāʾ) and warning (taḥdhīr):
1- Taḥdhīr is a manner of speech by which the addressee is alerted to a disliked matter so that he avoids it.
2- Ighrāʾ is a manner of speech by which the addressee is encouraged to a praiseworthy matter so that he undertakes it.
3- The two manners, taḥdhīr and ighrāʾ, share the following forms:
(a) That the thing warned against and the thing incited to is mentioned as a single word, accusative by an omitted verb, permissibly, such as:
(الكذب فإنه طريق الشر) i.e. "beware of lying", (الصدق فإنه طريق البرّ) i.e. "keep to truthfulness". Here omission of the verb is permissible, that is, mentioning it is not wrong.
(b) That each of them occurs repeated, such as (الكذب الكذب فإنه طريق الفجور), (الصدق الصدق فإنه طريق البر).
(c) That each of them occurs with a conjoined noun, such as (الأمانة والإحسان فإنهما من خلق المؤمن) (الكذب والغشّ فإنهما طريق الهلاك). In the last two cases (b, c) omission of the verb is obligatory. We parse the noun as accusative by ighrāʾ and taḥdhīr; if it is repeated, we parse the repeated one as a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī) with no grammatical position, while the conjoined one is a noun conjoined to the one incited to or warned against.
Taḥdhīr alone has one form, namely its being introduced by the accusative pronoun (إيّاك) and its derivatives: إياكما- إياكم- إياكن- ... etc.), after which comes the thing warned against, conjoined to it or put in the genitive with من, such as: (إياك والكذب) or (إياك من الكذب). We parse إياك: in the position of accusative by taḥdhīr, and الكذب: the wāw is a conjunction; الكذب is a direct object of an omitted verb, its implied form being "avoid", i.e. ("beware, you, and avoid lying").

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {وَضُحَاهَا}: The discussion of this root has already been given in [Sūrat] «Ṭā Hā». Al-Mubarrad said: «الضُّحى and الضَّحْوة are both derived from الضَّحّ, which is light; the alif and the wāw were substituted for the ḥāʾ.» This almost amounts to a fabrication against someone like Abū al-ʿAbbās, given his eminence.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {يَغْشَاهَا}: The object [pronoun] is for the sun; it was also said: for the earth. «يَغْشاها» was brought as an imperfect, unlike what precedes and follows it, out of regard for the verse-endings (fawāṣil); for had it been brought as a past, the construction would be «إذا غَشِيَها», and the verbal correspondence between the verse-endings and the cadences would be lost.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {وَمَا بَنَاهَا} and what follows it contain two views. The first: «ما» is a relative noun meaning «الذي» (who/which); those who permit its being used for individual rational beings cited it as evidence, because what is meant by it is the Creator, Exalted is He. Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid and Abū ʿUbayda held this, and Ibn Jarīr chose it. The second: it is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), i.e. "and the building of the heaven"; al-Zajjāj and al-Mubarrad held this, based on their view that it is restricted to non-rational beings. This view was objected to on the grounds that it would entail the oath being by the verbal nouns themselves: the building of the heaven, the spreading of the earth and the fashioning of the soul, whereas what is intended is only the oath by the doer of these things, namely the Lord, Blessed and Exalted. Two answers were given to this. The first: it is by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and by the Lord of — or the Builder of — the building of the heaven", and the like. The second: there is nothing strange in swearing by these things, just as He the Exalted swore by the morning and the like.
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It was made maṣdariyya, but this is not the right view, because of His saying "فأَلْهمها" and the corruption of the composition it leads to. The right view is that it is relative; it was preferred to "مَنْ" only to convey the meaning of description, as if it were said: and by the heaven and the Mighty, Powerful One Who built it, and by a soul and the Wise One of dazzling wisdom Who fashioned it. And among their sayings is: "سبحانَ ما سَخَّرَكُنَّ لنا" (Glory be to Him Who subjected you to us).» End of quotation. He means that the fāʿil (agent) in «فألهمها» refers to Allah the Exalted, so let it be so in «بناها» too; and then it must refer back to something, and there is nothing here to which it could refer except «ما», so it is determined that it is relative.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: «As for his saying: "it is not the right view because of His saying فَأَلْهمها", he means the reference of the pronoun in "فَأَلْهمها" to Allah the Exalted, so that it would refer to something mentioned, namely "ما" meant as "الذي". This does not follow, because if we make it maṣdariyya, the pronoun refers to what is understood from the context of the speech; so in "بناها" there is a pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, i.e. "and His building it", i.e. Allah the Exalted; just as, when you see Zayd having struck ʿAmr, you say: "عجبتُ مِمَّا ضَرَبَ عمراً", its implied form being: "at his striking ʿAmr" — this would be good, eloquent and permissible; and the reference of a pronoun to what is understood from the context of speech is frequent. And his saying: "and the corruption of the composition it leads to" is not so; making it maṣdariyya does not lead to what he mentioned. And his saying: "it was preferred only…" to the end — neither the relative "ما" nor the relative "مَنْ" conveys the meaning of description, because neither is used as an adjective, unlike "الذي"; so their sharing in not conveying the meaning of description is present in both, and "ما" does not have it to the exclusion of "مَنْ". And his saying: "and among their sayings…" to the end — our colleagues interpreted it as "سبحان" being a proper name and "ما" being maṣdariyya ẓarfiyya (temporal-verbal).» End of quotation.
As for his rebuttal of him by [the pronoun's] referring to what is understood from the context, it is not suitable as a rebuttal, because when the matter wavers between its referring to something expressed and something not expressed, its referring to what is expressed is preferable, because that is the basic rule. As for his saying: "so «ما» does not have it to the exclusion of «مَنْ»", al-Zamakhsharī does not mean that it is used as an explicit adjective; rather, he means that it applies to the kind of rational beings and to their attribute; that is why the grammarians illustrated it with His saying: {فانكحوا مَا طَابَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 3], and they said: its implied form is "so marry the good among women"; and there is no doubt that «ما» has this rule to the exclusion of «مَنْ». The indefiniteness of «نفس»: either it is to magnify it, i.e. a mighty soul, namely the soul of Ādam, or for multiplicity, as in His saying: {عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ} [al-Infiṭār: 5].

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {جَلاَّهَا}: The agent is a pronoun referring to the day (النهار). It was also said: it refers to Allah the Exalted. The accusative pronoun refers either to the sun, or to the darkness, or to the world (al-dunyā), or to the earth.

His saying: {إِذَا تَلاَهَا} and what follows it contain a difficulty. For if it is made conditional, it requires an apodosis, and there is no apodosis in the wording, and supplying one is not suitable. And if it is made a pure adverb, it calls for a governor, and there is no governor here except the verb of the oath; yet making it govern is problematic, because the verb of the oath is of the present (ḥāl), being a performative (inshāʾ), while «إذا» is an adverb of the future, and the present does not govern the future. The answer to this, and its verification, will come when I mention its probing and division (sabr and taqsīm) shortly, if Allah the Exalted wills.

The second «إذا» and what follows it have a further difficulty of their own, mentioned by al-Zamakhsharī, in which there is some obscurity, so take note of it. He said: "If you say: the matter of the accusative of «إذا» is baffling, because you cannot avoid one of two things. Either you make the wāws conjunctions, so that they cause accusative and genitive and you fall into conjunction upon two governors, as in your saying «مررتُ أمسِ بزيدٍ واليومَ عمروٍ» ("I passed yesterday by Zayd and today ʿAmr"); or you make them wāws of oath, so that you fall into what al-Khalīl and Sībawayh agreed to dislike. I say: the answer is that with the wāw of oath, expressing the verb is dropped altogether. So it has a status unlike that of the bāʾ, where the verb is expressed with it and also omitted; the wāw stands in the place of the verb, while the bāʾ fills the place of both together. The conjunctive wāws are deputies of this wāw, and so they rightly act as governors with the action of the verb and the preposition together, as you say «ضربَ زيدٌ عمراً وبكرٌ خالداً» ("Zayd struck ʿAmr and Bakr Khālid"), where you make nominative and accusative by the wāw, because it stands in the place of «ضرب», which is the governor of both." End of quotation.

The Shaykh [Translator's note: Abū Ḥayyān] said: "As for his saying about the conjunctive wāws 'so that they cause accusative and genitive': this is not the preferred view, I mean that the conjunction particle should govern by standing in the place of the governor. Rather, the preferred view is that the government belongs to the governor of the word conjoined to, and we do not dispute with him over that. As for his saying 'so you fall into conjunction upon two governors': what is in the verse is not conjunction upon two governors. It belongs rather to the chapter of conjoining two nouns, one genitive and one accusative, to two nouns, one genitive and one accusative, so the conjunction particle did not stand in for two governors. That is like your saying «امرُرْ بزيدٍ قائماً وعمروٍ جالساً» ("Pass by Zayd standing and ʿAmr sitting"). And Sībawayh recited in his book:

4578 - وليس بمعروفٍ لنا أَنْ نَرُدَّها ... صِحاحاً ولا مُسْتَنْكرٍ أن تُعَقَّرا
(It is not known among us that we return them sound, nor is it unheard of that they be hamstrung)

This is a conjunction of a genitive and a nominative upon a genitive and a nominative. Concerning conjunction upon two governors there are four doctrines, and permissibility is attributed to Sībawayh. As for his saying 'and in your saying «مررْتُ أمسِ بزيدٍ واليومَ عمروٍ»': this example differs from what is in the verse; rather the counterpart of what is in the verse is «مررْتُ بزيدٍ أمسٍ وعمروٍ اليومَ», and we permit this. As for his saying 'what al-Khalīl and Sībawayh agreed to dislike': it is not as he said; rather the speech of al-Khalīl indicates prohibition. Al-Khalīl said, concerning the saying of the Mighty and Exalted:

{والليل إِذَا يغشى والنهار إِذَا تجلى وَمَا خَلَقَ الذكر والأنثى} [al-Layl: 13]

'The last two wāws are not on the level of the first. They are the two wāws that join nouns to nouns, as in your saying «مررتُ بزيدٍ وعمرو», whereas the first is on the level of the tāʾ and the bāʾ.' As for his saying that the wāw of oath is one with which expressing the verb is dropped altogether: this ruling is not agreed upon; rather Ibn Kaysān permitted stating the verb of the oath with the wāw, so you say «أُقْسِم» or «أَحْلِفُ» «واللَّهِ لَزيدٌ قائمٌ». And as for his saying 'the conjunctive wāws are deputies of this one' to the end: it is built on the claim that the conjunction particle governs because it stands in for the governor, and that is not the preferred view." He said: "What we say is that the baffling thing is supplying the governor of «إذا» after the oaths, as in His saying {والنجم إِذَا هوى} [al-Najm: 1], {والليل إِذْ أَدْبَرَ} [al-Muddaththir: 33], {والصبح إِذَآ أَسْفَرَ} [al-Muddaththir: 34], {والقمر إِذَا تَلاَهَا}, {والليل إِذَا يغشى} [al-Layl: 1], and the like. For «إذا» is an adverb of the future. It cannot be that its governor is the omitted verb of the oath, because that is a performative verb and so is of the present, and it is incompatible for it to govern the future, owing to the difference between the time of the governor and the time of the governed. Nor can there be an omitted muḍāf with the thing sworn by standing in its place, i.e. 'and by the rising of the star and the coming of the night', because that is governed by that verb; the rising is of the present, and it does not govern the future, since of necessity the time of the governor is the time of the governed. Nor can the thing sworn by itself govern it, because it is not among the things that govern, especially if it is a body. Nor can an omitted word be supplied before the adverb so that it governs it, that governor being in the position of a ḥāl, its implied form being 'by the star, being [there] when it falls; by the night, being [there] when it covers', because it would follow that «كائناً» has no governor to put it in the accusative, and it cannot be governed by any of the things we supposed to be governors. Moreover the thing sworn by may be a body, and adverbs of time cannot be ḥāls of bodies, just as they cannot be predicates." End of what the Shaykh used in refutation, and of what he found problematic regarding the governor of «إذا». And I, praise be to Allah, shall follow his statements and make clear what is in them.

[The author:] As for his saying "the preferred view is that the conjunction particle does not govern by standing in the place of the governor": this does not bind Abū al-Qāsim [Translator's note: al-Zamakhsharī], because he prefers the other view. As for his saying "what is in this verse is not conjunction upon two governors": that is disputed; rather it does contain conjunction upon two governors, though with some obscurity. The explanation that it is conjunction upon two governors is as follows: His saying {والنهار إِذَا جَلاَّهَا} has here two governed words, one genitive, namely «النهار», and the other accusative, namely the adverb. This is a conjunction upon the two governed words of two governors, the two governors being the verb of the oath which puts the first «إذا» in the accusative, and the wāw of oath which causes the genitive. So you have two governors, each with a governed word. When you conjoin a genitive to a genitive and an adverb to an adverb, as two governed words of two governors, what Abū al-Qāsim said follows. How could this be missed by anyone who reflects and verifies?

As for his saying "and Sībawayh recited …" to the end: that is an admission from him that it is a case of conjunction upon two governors; the most he did was to lean on the standing of Sībawayh.

As for his saying "Ibn Kaysān permitted …": his doctrine does not bind al-Zamakhsharī. As for his saying "the example corresponds to the verse; rather its counterpart is …" to the end: that is correct, because in it the second adverb is put before the conjoined genitive, whereas in the verse the adverb comes later. But what al-Zamakhsharī means is the existence of two governed words of two governors, and that exists in the example he mentioned, except that it has another difficulty, namely that it is like a repetition of the issue.

As for his saying "rather the speech of al-Khalīl indicates prohibition" to the end: there is no refutation of him in it with regard to what he intended; rather it strengthens what he said. The most there is, is that he expressed prohibition by "dislike," or did not understand the prohibition. As for his saying "nor can there be an omitted muḍāf" to the end, I say: rather, supplying it is permissible, and it is the governor, and the difference of the two times that he claimed does not follow. For it is permissible to swear now by the rising of the star in the future, so the oath is in the present and the rising in the future; and it is permissible to swear by something that will come into existence. As for his saying "nor can an omitted word be supplied before the adverb so that it governs it" to the end: that is not prohibited; rather it is permissible, and it is an implied (muqaddara) ḥāl. As for his saying "it would follow that it has no governor": it is not so; rather it has a governor, namely the verb of the oath, and its being a performative does no harm, because the ḥāl is implied, as already stated. As for his saying "the thing sworn by may be a body": the answer is that an event is then supplied of which the adverb of time is a ḥāl. This question was put to the Shaykh Abū ʿAmr Ibn al-Ḥājib, who refined the question and answered along the lines of what I mentioned. And Allah knows best. Yet the discussion of it is not free of dispute and long debate with him.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {قَدْ أَفْلَحَ}: There are two views on it. One: that it is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), the original being «لقد», and the lām was omitted only because of the length of the speech. The second: that it is not an answer, but was brought as a follower to His saying {فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَاهَا} by way of digression (istiṭrād), and is in no way part of the answer to the oath. The answer is then omitted, its implied form being «ليُدَمْدِمَنَّ اللَّهُ عليهم» ("Allah will surely crush them"), i.e. the people of Mecca, for their denial of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, just as He crushed Thamūd for their denial of Ṣāliḥ, peace be upon him. Al-Zamakhsharī gave this sense, while others supplied «لتُبْعَثُنَّ» ("you will surely be resurrected").

And His saying: {طَحَاهَا} [al-Shams: 3], i.e. «دَحاها» ("spread it out"); its meaning has already been given. It has two forms: one says «طحا يَطْحوا» and «طحى يَطْحي». «طحا» also comes in the sense of "went away". ʿAlqama said:

4579 - طحابك قَلْبٌ في الحِسانِ طَروبُ ... بُعَيْدَ الشبابِ عَصْرَ حان مَشيبُ
(A heart addicted to fair women has carried you away, just after youth, at the time when grey hair has come)

It is also said that «طحا» means "rose high". Among their oaths is «ولا والقمرِ الطَّاحي», i.e. "the one rising high". As for the agent of «زكَّاها» and «دَسَّاها», the apparent sense is that it is the pronoun of «مَنْ». It was also said: it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, i.e. "whoever Allah purified" and "whoever Allah corrupted," meaning: whoever Allah has purified his soul. Al-Zamakhsharī attacked the holder of this view because it clashes with his own school. The truth is that it is contrary to the apparent sense, not for the reason al-Zamakhsharī gave, but because it clashes with the structure of the wording, since it requires the pronoun to return to the soul as qualified by its being annexed to the pronoun of «مَنْ»

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {دَسَّاهَا}: Its origin is «دسَّسَهَا». The like letters became too many, so a weak letter was substituted for the third of them, as they said «قَصَّيْتُ [أَظْفاري]» ("I trimmed my nails") and [in the saying]:

4580 - تَقَضِّيَ البازِي. . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(The swooping of the falcon … [the rest of the verse is omitted in the source])

[Translator's note: the rest of the verse is left blank with dots in the source.] And «التَّدْسِيَةُ» is concealment, meaning: he concealed it with immorality. The original form was actually pronounced by the one who said:

4581 - وأنت الذي دَسَّسْتَ عمراً فأصبحَتْ ... حَلائلُه منه أراملَ ضُيَّعاً
(It was you who buried ʿAmr, so his wives became, because of it, widows, forsaken)

and by the one who said:

4582 - ودَسَّسْت عَمْراً في التراب فأصبحَتْ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(And I buried ʿAmr in the dust, so … [the rest is omitted in the source])

the verse [in full].

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {بِطَغْوَاهَآ}: This bāʾ has three possible senses. The first: that it is the bāʾ of instrumentality (istiʿāna) in a figurative sense, as in "I wrote with the pen." Al-Zamakhsharī began with this, and he means: it denied by means of its transgression, as you say, "He wronged me by his audacity against Allah the Exalted." The second: that it is a bāʾ of transitivity (taʿdiya), i.e. it denied what it was threatened with, namely its punishment, the punishment of transgression, as in His saying, the Exalted, {فَأُهْلِكُواْ بالطاغية} [al-Ḥāqqa: 5]. The third: that it is for causation, i.e. because of its transgression.

The majority read «طَغْواها» with fatḥa on the ṭāʾ; it is a maṣdar meaning «الطُّغيان» ("transgression"). The yāʾ was turned into a wāw only in order to distinguish the noun from the adjective. That is, they keep the yāʾ of the pattern fa‘lā with fatḥa when it is an adjective, such as «خَزْيا» and «صَدْيا», and they change it in the noun, such as «تَقْوى» and «شَرْوى». The yāʾ was kept in the adjective because the adjective is heavier than the noun, and the yāʾ is lighter than the wāw, so it was placed in the heavier.

Al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad b. Kaʿb and Ḥammād read it with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ; this too is a maṣdar like «الرُّجْعى» and «الحُسْنى», except that it is irregular (shādhdh), since by right the yāʾ should have stayed as it is, like «السُّقْيا» and its like. All this holds for those who say «طَغَيْتُ طُغْياناً» with yāʾ. As for those who say «طَغَوْت» with wāw, for them the wāw is the original. Abū al-Baqāʾ said this. The discussion of the two dialects has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, and praise be to Allah.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إِذِ انبعث}: «إذِ» admits two analyses. One: that it is an adverb attached to «كذَّبَتْ». The second: that it is an adverb attached to «الطَّغْوى».

«أشْقاها» is the agent of «انبعَث». It has two views. One: that a single, specific person is meant. In the exegesis it is a man called Qudār b. Sālif. The second: that a group is meant. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It may be that they were a group, and the singular is because you treat the singular and the plural, the masculine and the feminine, alike in the elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) when you annex it. It would have been possible to say «أشْقَوْها»." End of quotation. He ought to have qualified it by saying "when you annex it to a definite noun," because the ruling for an elative annexed to an indefinite noun is the singular and the masculine in every case, like the one accompanied by «مِنْ».

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {فَقَالَ لَهُمْ}: If «أَشْقاها» means a group, the return of the pronoun in «لهم» to them is clear; if it means a specific individual, then the pronoun in «لهم» refers to Thamūd.

His saying: {نَاقَةَ الله} is accusative as a warning (taḥdhīr), i.e. "beware of the she-camel of Allah, and do not approach her." Omitting the governing verb is obligatory here because of the conjunction, for omitting the governor is obligatory in three places. First: when the one warned against is of the type «إيّاك» and its class. Second: when a conjunction is present. Third: when a repetition is present, such as «الأسدَ الأسدَ».

Zayd b. ʿAlī read «ناقةُ الله» in the nominative, as the predicate of an implied subject, i.e. "this is the she-camel of Allah, so do not expose yourselves to her."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {فَدَمْدَمَ}: As for «الدَّمْدَمَةُ», it was said: it is covering over; one says «دَمْدَمْتُ عليه القبرَ», i.e. "I covered the grave over him." It was said: it is pressing to the ground. It was said: destruction by uprooting. It was said: «الدَّمْدَمَةُ» is an imitation of the sound of a crash, and from it comes «دَمْدَمَ في كلامه» ("he muttered in his speech"). And «دَمْدَمْتُ الثوبَ» means "I coated the garment with dye." The bāʾ in «بذَنْبهم» is for causation.

His saying: {فَسَوَّاهَا}: The accusative pronoun may refer to Thamūd, regarded as a tribe, as it was made to refer in His saying «بَطَغْواها»; and it may refer to the crushing and the punishment, i.e. "He made it equal among them," so none of them escaped. Ibn al-Zubayr read «فَدَهْدَمَ», with a hāʾ between the two dāls in place of the mīm, which means the same as the well-known reading.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يَخَافُ}: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read «فلا» with fāʾ, and the others with wāw. It is written with fāʾ in the copies of Medina and Syria and with wāw in the others, so each read according to what agrees with the script of his own codex. It is reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to read «ولم يَخَفْ», which supports the reading with wāw; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned it. The fāʾ requires sequence, which is obvious.
